project.name: dotfiles
project.description: Personal dotfiles for mryfmo, managed with chezmoi, providing a zsh/sheldon/starship/mise shell environment, Claude Code and Codex agent configuration, herdr/agmsg orchestration tooling, install scripts, and bats tests. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: CompactionDB command-line interface (contextdb_cli) exposing recent/prompts/search/show/files/sessions/recover/probe/recall/health/drain/verify/prune/export/ingest and a memory subcommand family over the SQLite ledger.

nodes.name: _add_scope
nodes.summary: Adds --session/--scope arguments to a subparser.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Builds the argparse tree for all contextdb CLI subcommands and the nested memory subcommands.

nodes.name: _format_event
nodes.summary: Formats an event row as a single display line.

nodes.name: _resolve_session
nodes.summary: Resolves the requested or latest session id, enforcing an explicit session for session scope.

nodes.name: _rows_json
nodes.summary: Converts sqlite rows to plain dicts for JSON output.

nodes.name: _print_json_or_lines
nodes.summary: Prints a value as pretty JSON or as text lines depending on --json.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Dispatches a parsed CLI command to ingest, drain, query, recover, probe, recall, health, verify, prune or export operations on the ContextStore.

nodes.name: _run_memory
nodes.summary: Handles memory subcommands: list, search, candidates, promote, add, retract, embed, semantic-search and compact.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses argv, runs the command and maps errors to an exit code.

nodes.name: probe.py
nodes.summary: Generates recovery-quality probes (first error, modified files, decisions, open tasks) with ground-truth answers from a session's ledger, used to evaluate compaction recovery.

nodes.name: generate_probes
nodes.summary: Builds recall/artifact/decision/task probe questions with ground truth from the session's events and memories.

nodes.name: recall.py
nodes.summary: Hybrid recall engine fusing FTS5 lexical scores and optional embedding similarity over events and memories, then expanding event hits through tool_use_id and adjacency closures.
nodes.languageNotes: Score fusion is rho*lexical + (1-rho)*semantic after min-max normalization, falling back to lexical-only when embeddings are unavailable.

nodes.name: normalize_scores
nodes.summary: Min-max normalizes a score dict to [0,1].

nodes.name: _key
nodes.summary: Builds a record_type:id key for a result row.

nodes.name: _event
nodes.summary: Converts an event row into a recall result dict.

nodes.name: _memory
nodes.summary: Converts a memory row into a recall result dict.

nodes.name: _lexical
nodes.summary: Runs FTS5 BM25 lexical search over events and current memories and returns rows with raw scores.

nodes.name: _semantic
nodes.summary: Runs embedding similarity search over memories when semantic search is enabled.

nodes.name: _closure
nodes.summary: Collects related events for a hit via shared tool_use_id and adjacent events in the same session.

nodes.name: recall
nodes.summary: Fuses lexical and semantic scores, ranks results and expands event hits with closure neighbours at inherited score up to k results.

nodes.name: recovery.py
nodes.summary: Builds the bounded post-compaction recovery packet (goal, file modifications, recent activity, decisions, open tasks, failures, compact summary) from the session ledger and curated memories.

nodes.name: _detail
nodes.summary: Parses a row's detail_json into a dict, tolerating malformed JSON.

nodes.name: _modified_files
nodes.summary: Summarizes written/edited files for a session with last operation and counts within a character budget.

nodes.name: _render_packet
nodes.summary: Renders the recovery header and sections within the total and file-section budgets.

nodes.name: build_recovery_context
nodes.summary: Assembles the post-compaction recovery packet from prompts, events, failures, files, memories and the compact summary.

nodes.name: semantic.py
nodes.summary: Optional semantic-search adapter that runs a configured external embedding command over JSON stdin/stdout and provides cosine similarity.

nodes.name: SemanticConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding semantic-search settings: enabled flag, command, model, timeout and batch size.

nodes.name: semantic_config
nodes.summary: Parses and validates the semantic section of the config into a SemanticConfig.

nodes.name: embed_texts
nodes.summary: Runs the configured embedding command over JSON stdin and validates the returned vectors.

nodes.name: cosine_similarity
nodes.summary: Computes cosine similarity between two vectors.

nodes.name: storage.py
nodes.summary: SQLite storage layer for CompactionDB: schema with events, sessions, file refs, memory candidates, memories, embeddings and hierarchical memory blocks plus FTS5 indexes, and the ContextStore API for ingest, search, memory lifecycle, health, verification and retention.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses SQLite FTS5 virtual tables with a trigram-or-unicode61 tokenizer probe and WAL journaling; schema is an embedded DDL string.

nodes.name: ContextStore
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed store for the CompactionDB ledger and durable memories, owning schema, FTS indexes, ingestion, queries, memory lifecycle, embeddings, health and retention.

nodes.name: connect

nodes.name: secure_storage_files
nodes.summary: Restricts permissions on the database and WAL/SHM files.

nodes.name: _ensure_fts
nodes.summary: Creates the events and memories FTS5 virtual tables with a trigram or unicode61 tokenizer.

nodes.name: insert_event

nodes.name: retract_memory

nodes.name: current_memories

nodes.name: rebuild_memory_blocks

nodes.name: _insert_block

nodes.name: hierarchical_memory_context

nodes.name: recent_files

nodes.name: search_events

nodes.name: search_memories
nodes.summary: Full-text searches current memories.

nodes.name: promote_candidate
nodes.summary: Promotes a memory candidate into a durable memory.

nodes.name: index_memory_embeddings

nodes.name: semantic_search_memories

nodes.name: health

nodes.name: export_events

nodes.name: main

nodes.name: _sentences

nodes.name: extract_candidates

nodes.name: compress_lines

nodes.name: _tool_summary

nodes.name: _relative_path

nodes.name: _extract_file_refs

nodes.name: encode_detail
nodes.summary: Bounds a detail value to a character budget, truncating fields and recording hashes.

nodes.name: normalize_hook_payload
nodes.summary: Turns a raw hook payload into a normalized, redacted ledger event with summary, file refs, memory candidates and retention expiry.

nodes.name: redaction.py

nodes.name: RedactionReport

nodes.name: is_sensitive_path

nodes.name: _replacement

nodes.name: redact_text

nodes.name: find_paths

nodes.name: redact_value

nodes.name: sanitize_payload

nodes.name: ensure_dir

nodes.name: safe_chmod

nodes.name: _write_all

nodes.name: _fsync_directory

nodes.name: write_text_exclusive

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Ubuntu 24.04 test-container image that creates a passwordless-sudo user matching the host UID/GID, sets the Asia/Tokyo timezone, and installs chezmoi with the chezmoi source directory as the working directory for trying the dotfiles bootstrap in isolation.
nodes.languageNotes: Reuses or renames any existing group/user with the requested UID/GID (Ubuntu 24.04 ships a default ubuntu user at 1000) instead of failing on useradd.

nodes.name: ubuntu
nodes.summary: Single-stage build based on ubuntu:24.04 that installs curl, git, sudo, tzdata, parallel and build-essential and prepares the non-root dotfiles user.

nodes.name: agent-assets.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that validates agent, MCP, plugin and skill assets with validate-agent-assets.py and parses .coderabbit.yaml on PRs/pushes to main, plus a weekly scheduled check of upstream Codex/Claude documentation links and npm package versions.

nodes.name: docs.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that, on pushes to main touching docs-relevant paths, installs uv and mise tools and runs `make deploy` to build and publish the MkDocs reference site to GitHub Pages.

nodes.name: macos.yaml
nodes.summary: macOS (M1) CI workflow that bootstraps the dotfiles via setup.sh with private dotfiles secrets, verifies a rerun refuses local drift, runs and publishes a shell startup benchmark, and checks deployed files with bats.

nodes.name: remote.yaml
nodes.summary: Weekly and PR workflow that exercises the remote setup.sh bootstrap against the checked-out commit in an isolated HOME across Ubuntu client/server and macOS client matrices, asserting unmanaged sentinel files keep their content and modes, with an optional private-dotfiles bootstrap job.

nodes.name: test.yaml
nodes.summary: Required unit-test workflow: a change-detection job gates a macOS/Ubuntu matrix that installs tools, smoke-tests statusline tools offline, runs shfmt/ShellCheck, Python unittests (make unit-test) and bats unit tests with bashcov coverage uploaded to Codecov, plus a Nix job evaluating flake home-manager and nix-darwin outputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentionally has no workflow-level path filters so required checks always report; relevance is decided inside a changes job via job outputs.

nodes.name: ubuntu.yaml
nodes.summary: Ubuntu CI workflow that bootstraps the dotfiles via setup.sh for client and server systems, verifies a rerun rejects local drift, and validates deployed files with tag-filtered bats suites.

nodes.name: .coderabbit.yaml
nodes.summary: CodeRabbit review configuration: Japanese review prose with English code, request-changes workflow, path filters excluding .orchestration/, reviews/ and .ua/, and automatic reviews disabled so reviews run only on explicit `@coderabbitai full review` requests.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Canonical cross-runtime agent instruction file covering chezmoi repository context, ADH release-set rules, comment policy, git/PR workflow, test policy, Crit review evidence, standing auditor rules and dotfiles-safety code-review rules.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Claude-only shim that imports AGENTS.md and carries the CompactionDB context-recovery block with contextdb_cli.py commands for sessions, events and durable memory.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: Repository lifecycle entry point with targets for Docker testing, chezmoi setup/init/update/apply (including private dotfiles, agent asset refresh, Herdr config reload and agmsg bootstrap), doctor/upgrade, usage reports, validation and review gates, and MkDocs docs build/serve/deploy.
nodes.languageNotes: The update target only pulls when on a clean main tracking origin/main, then applies chezmoi and classifies `herdr status server --json` with jq before reloading config.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive project README with 27 sections covering macOS/Ubuntu setup, individual app installs, mosh and private credentials, lifecycle commands (update/doctor/upgrade), agent review and permission assets, Claude Code sandbox, agmsg, Herdr/Ghostty agent workspaces, the PR feedback merge gate, and Docker/bats/Codecov testing.

nodes.name: codecov.yml
nodes.summary: Codecov configuration that ignores Codex skill assets and itself and sets an automatic project coverage target with a 1% threshold for shell unit-test coverage.

nodes.name: mise.toml
nodes.summary: Root-level mise configuration containing only an empty [tools] table, so the repository root declares no project-local tool pins.

nodes.name: mkdocs.yml
nodes.summary: MkDocs Material site configuration for the generated dotfiles reference docs, enabling search and toc-md catalog generation, extra CSS, and code-highlighting markdown extensions.

nodes.name: renovate.json
nodes.summary: Renovate dependency-update policy for GitHub Actions, mise tools and regex-matched agent-config.yaml asset pins, grouping minor/patch updates, requiring dashboard approval for pins that make upgrade must recompute, and disabling fd updates.

nodes.name: setup.sh
nodes.summary: Public bootstrap script for macOS and Ubuntu that installs Homebrew from a pinned, checksum-verified installer on macOS, downloads a checksum-verified pinned chezmoi release, and runs chezmoi init/update/apply while refusing to overwrite local drift or apply outside RUNNER_TEMP in CI.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with set -Eeuo pipefail, an at_exit helper that accumulates EXIT traps, and a BASH_SOURCE guard so tests can source it without running main.

nodes.name: fetch_url
nodes.summary: Streams a URL to stdout using curl or falling back to wget, failing when neither is available.

nodes.name: fetch_file
nodes.summary: Downloads a URL to a destination file, preferring curl over wget and failing when neither exists.

nodes.name: verify_sha256
nodes.summary: Verifies a file against an expected SHA-256 digest, failing on a missing checksum or mismatch.

nodes.name: keepalive_sudo_linux
nodes.summary: Primes sudo credentials on Linux and keeps them alive with a background refresh loop for the bootstrap duration.

nodes.name: keepalive_sudo_macos
nodes.summary: Primes sudo credentials on macOS and keeps them alive in the background without storing the password in Keychain.

nodes.name: keepalive_sudo
nodes.summary: Starts the OS-appropriate sudo keepalive once per run, dispatching to the macOS or Linux variant.

nodes.name: initialize_os_macos
nodes.summary: Installs Homebrew non-interactively from a pinned commit after verifying the installer SHA-256, then loads brew shellenv from the detected prefix.

nodes.name: initialize_os_env
nodes.summary: Runs OS-specific initialization, delegating to the macOS Homebrew setup or the no-op Linux step.

nodes.name: run_chezmoi
nodes.summary: Downloads and checksum-verifies the pinned chezmoi binary for the platform, runs chezmoi init and update, strips age-encrypted files in non-TTY runs, refuses to apply when local drift or an unsafe CI HOME is detected, applies, and removes the temporary binary.

nodes.name: initialize_dotfiles
nodes.summary: Starts the sudo keepalive for interactive TTY runs and then runs the chezmoi bootstrap.

nodes.name: restart_shell_system
nodes.summary: Execs a login zsh for client systems or login bash for server systems based on chezmoi data, rejecting unknown system values.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Script entry point that prints the logo, initializes the OS environment, and bootstraps the dotfiles.

nodes.name: config.json
nodes.summary: Understand-Anything project settings: sets English output and turns off automatic graph updates, so the plugin's SessionStart and PostToolUse update prompts stay silent. The graph is refreshed only by explicit full rebuilds.

nodes.name: fingerprints.json
nodes.summary: Generated fingerprint baseline for the previous analysis (commit 72b8901, 365 files). It records each file's content hash, line count, and extracted functions, classes, imports, and exports, which Understand-Anything uses to detect changes.
nodes.languageNotes: Machine-generated JSON keyed by project-relative path, with top-level version, gitCommitHash, generatedAt and files. Do not edit by hand.

nodes.name: knowledge-graph.json
nodes.summary: The previously committed Understand-Anything knowledge graph for the dotfiles repo: 885 nodes, 1325 edges, 9 architectural layers, and a 15-step guided tour, with project metadata under `project`. Agents query it before repo-wide searches while it is fresh.
nodes.languageNotes: Machine-generated JSON with top-level version, project, nodes, edges, layers and tour. It is replaced wholesale by `/understand --full`.

nodes.name: meta.json
nodes.summary: Records metadata for the last graph analysis: timestamp, source git commit hash, schema version, and analyzed file count. Freshness checks compare its gitCommitHash with HEAD to decide whether the graph is current.

nodes.name: mise.sh
nodes.summary: Downloads a pinned standalone mise release for the current OS/architecture, verifies it against the upstream SHA256 manifest, installs it atomically into ~/.local/bin, then runs locked `mise install` passes for node, statusline tools, agent CLIs, and the remaining toolchain with a release-age cooldown.

nodes.name: verify_mise_archive
nodes.summary: Looks up the expected SHA256 for an artifact in the release checksum manifest and compares it with sha256sum/shasum output, failing on missing or mismatched checksums.

nodes.name: _install_mise_binary
nodes.summary: Subshell-scoped installer that downloads the pinned mise tarball and SHASUMS256.txt, verifies the checksum, extracts it, and atomically moves the binary into MISE_INSTALL_PATH with trap-based cleanup.

nodes.name: run_mise_install
nodes.summary: Trusts the repo mise config and runs staged `mise install --locked` passes: node, statusline npm tools, agent CLIs with the npm min-release-age bypass, then everything else with a 7-day `--before` cooldown.

nodes.name: sheldon.sh
nodes.summary: Builds and installs the pinned Sheldon shell plugin manager from crates.io via `mise exec -- cargo install --locked`, staging the binary and moving it atomically into ~/.local/bin.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a subshell-bodied function so the EXIT trap scopes cleanup; the Sheldon version is rendered from agent-config.yaml.

nodes.name: install_sheldon

nodes.name: install_homebrew

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README, which explains that this is a chezmoi-managed dotfiles repository targeting macOS, Ubuntu Desktop (client) and Ubuntu Server (server), and documents setup snippets, the update/doctor/upgrade lifecycle, and the agent tooling. AGENTS.md is the canonical instruction file for every AI runtime working on the repo, so reading both gives you the human and the agent view of the same project before any code.

tour.title: The Remote Bootstrap
tour.description: setup.sh is the one-line entry point that the README's curl snippets run: it installs a pinned, checksum-verified Homebrew on macOS, downloads a verified chezmoi release, and runs chezmoi init/apply while refusing to overwrite local drift. The tiny .chezmoiroot marker tells chezmoi that the real source state lives under home/, which is why almost every other file in this tour sits in that directory.

tour.title: chezmoi Source-State Control
tour.description: Once setup.sh hands off to chezmoi, these templates decide what a given machine receives. .chezmoi.yaml.tmpl resolves identity, the client/server role and the private-layer opt-in; .chezmoiignore composes per-OS ignore fragments (the common fragment shown here) so each machine gets only relevant files; and .chezmoiexternal.yaml.tmpl pulls in checksummed external archives per OS.
tour.languageLesson: chezmoi encodes target attributes in source file names: dot_zshrc becomes ~/.zshrc, executable_ sets the exec bit, private_ restricts permissions, symlink_ creates a link, modify_ runs a script that transforms the existing target, and a .tmpl suffix renders the file through Go text/template with chezmoi data such as .chezmoi.os.

tour.title: Run-Once Installer Steps
tour.description: chezmoi scripts under .chezmoiscripts run around the file-apply phase: the run_once_before script decrypts the age identity needed for private files, and run_once_after wrappers such as install-mise inline real installer logic from install/. The install/ scripts (mise, Homebrew on macOS, apt dependencies on Ubuntu) all follow the same pattern of downloading pinned artifacts and verifying SHA256 before installing.
tour.languageLesson: chezmoi orders scripts by prefix: run_once_before_ runs before files are written and run_once_after_ after, run_once_ scripts run only once per content hash, run_onchange_ reruns whenever the script's rendered content changes, and the numeric part (01, 02, 99) sorts execution within each phase.

tour.title: Pinned Tools and Supply Chain
tour.description: The global mise manifest is one of the most depended-upon nodes in the graph (fan-in 11): it pins runtimes and CLIs such as Claude Code, Codex, herdr and gh with lockfile enforcement across four platforms. installer-pins.sh holds reviewed versions and checksums for non-mise installers, upgrade-tools.sh is the explicit lifecycle that bumps those pins, and Renovate proposes updates while requiring approval for pins that the upgrade flow must recompute.

tour.title: Shell Startup Chain
tour.description: With tools installed, the zsh startup files define the daily environment: .zshenv is a silent, minimal file every shell reads (including non-interactive SSH sessions for Mosh/Herdr), .zprofile handles login PATH setup, and .zshrc wires interactive behavior. Plugins are assembled by the sheldon template, which includes the common plugin source plus client or server sources depending on the chezmoi data from Step 3.
tour.languageLesson: zsh reads .zshenv for every shell, .zprofile for login shells and .zshrc for interactive shells, so keep .zshenv fast and side-effect free. sheldon's zsh-defer templates postpone plugin loading until after the first prompt, which is how a heavy plugin set still starts quickly.

tour.title: Prompt, Git, and Helpers
tour.description: On top of the shell, Starship renders the prompt and a custom segment shows how many commits the chezmoi source is behind origin/main, fed by the chezmoi-notify zsh plugin's hourly background check. The git config template takes its identity from chezmoi data and enforces SSH-signed commits, while the shared aliases and the dev helper (fuzzy-select a ghq repo and rename the tmux session) show the small quality-of-life tools layered on everyday work.

tour.title: Agent Config Single Source
tour.description: The agent side of the repository starts here. agent-config.yaml has the highest fan-in in the graph (22): it is the single hand-edited manifest for model profiles, worker settings, sandboxes, permissions, hooks and plugins for both Codex and Claude Code. generate-agent-configs.py (fan-in 16) renders it into agent-native files such as model-profiles.env and the Codex config modify script, and the dot_agents README documents that contract.

tour.title: Claude Settings and Rules
tour.description: Claude Code is configured the same way: claude-settings-managed.json is the generated baseline (model defaults, permission lists, bubblewrap sandbox and hooks), and the modify script merges it into the live ~/.claude/settings.json without losing state Claude itself owns. Global rules such as model-selection.md live once under dot_config/claude/rules and are symlinked into ~/.claude/rules, so the policies from Step 8's manifest are restated as instructions the agent actually loads.
tour.languageLesson: modify_private_settings.json is a Python script despite its .json name: chezmoi pipes the current target file to a modify_ script on stdin and writes its stdout back. That merge-with-live-state pattern lets dotfiles own the managed keys while the application keeps writing its own runtime keys to the same file.

tour.title: Agent Orchestration Executables
tour.description: These executables turn the configuration into a working multi-agent setup. herdr-agents builds and repairs the Herdr workspace with a Claude orchestrator pane and Codex/Claude worker panes, agmsg-dispatch delivers messages and wakes idle workers, and the agmsg-orchestration skill defines the task/result protocol they follow. permgate, driven by its policy file, is the PermissionRequest hook that applies deterministic deny/allow rules before anything else.

tour.title: CompactionDB Hook Ingestion
tour.description: CompactionDB keeps Claude Code sessions recoverable after context compaction. The project's .claude/settings.json registers a hook on every lifecycle event; the contextdb_hook.py shim delegates to hook.py, which normalizes each payload (normalize.py) and writes it to a durable spool (spool.py) before draining it into SQLite. The design never blocks the agent: capture is cheap and failure-tolerant.
tour.languageLesson: A spool-and-drain design writes each event to its own file with an exclusive create, then a single writer holding a file lock moves the events into SQLite. Hooks stay fast and crash-safe, and malformed records are quarantined instead of corrupting the database.

tour.title: CompactionDB Storage and Recovery
tour.description: Building on the ingestion path from Step 11, storage.py defines the SQLite schema (events, sessions, memories, FTS5 indexes) and the ContextStore API, while redaction.py strips secrets before anything is persisted. On SessionStart, recover_hook.py asks recovery.py to build a bounded recovery packet and injects it into the new context, and cli.py exposes the same ledger for searches, health checks and memory management.

tour.title: Makefile Lifecycle Tooling
tour.description: The Makefile (fan-out 16, the widest in the graph) is the operator's front door for setup, update, doctor, upgrade and validation. update-agent-assets.sh converges plugins and pinned releases, check-agent-runtime.py proves the live HOME matches the source tree, and the review gate pairs require-crit-review.py with pr-feedback.py so meaningful diffs and pull requests cannot merge without recorded review evidence.
tour.languageLesson: Make targets that do not produce files are declared .PHONY so make always runs them; a lifecycle Makefile like this one is mostly phony targets that sequence shell and Python scripts with shared variables.

tour.title: Validation and Tests
tour.description: validate-agent-assets.py checks repository-wide invariants for agents, hooks, sandboxes, model profiles, asset pins and secret hygiene, and it runs both locally and in CI. The Python suites enforce the supply-chain policy from Step 5 and the truthful runtime-health behavior from Step 13, run_unit_test.sh dispatches the bats suites per OS and role, and the Dockerfile provides an Ubuntu container for trying the dotfiles in isolation.

tour.title: CI Workflows Capstone
tour.description: GitHub Actions ties everything together. test.yaml gates a macOS/Ubuntu matrix of linting, Python unittests and bats coverage behind a change-detection job; ubuntu.yaml and macos.yaml run the real setup.sh bootstrap from Step 2 and check that a rerun refuses local drift; agent-assets.yml runs the validator from Step 14; and docs.yml publishes the MkDocs reference site.
tour.languageLesson: A change-detection job that emits outputs (for example via paths filters) lets later jobs use `needs` and `if` to skip expensive matrix builds when only unrelated files changed, while `strategy.matrix` fans one job definition out across operating systems.
